title: García de Toledo to Philip II, 16 July 1565 (Great Siege of Malta), AGS Estado leg. 1394 no. 247

steps.what: Worked out the PARES image route (cookie jar, dbCode, zoom 10) and fetched six images.
Transcribed the figure runs digit for digit with the clear text around them.
Runs beside clear words read as 'seiscientos' and 'en tiera', fixing a c d e i l n o r s t.
Key order is alphabetical, so the remaining letters (f, x, y, z) were predicted from their neighbours and confirmed in words.
Decoded the whole letter; nonsense in the output located misread digits, which were corrected on the images.
All groups in 12-43, all 32 used, no odd runs; names such as Provana di Leinì fit the Sicilian record for July 1565.

Found the same-day companion letter EST,LEG,1394,249 (duplicate, one page) by PARES search; its cipher runs decode with the same key (entrado el socorro, Cabo Bono, Argel, las galeras con la gente a la Goleta, partiran las galeras manana), adding a barred-theta sign for ll. Not read in full.

Novelty re-examined. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The key was rebuilt here from two cribs in the clear text, but it is easy and may have been recovered before; the claim is a reading of this letter, not a first break.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The alphabetical homophonic key (figures 12-43) was rebuilt from cribs in the clear Spanish around the figures in the letter itself; Tomokiyo's 'undeciphered' means no contemporary decipherment, and whether the key existed elsewhere is unknown.
outcome.notes: Open word readings only (yaretas, secanos); every group has a value.

prior.where: Tomokiyo lists 1565 Malta cipher letters as undeciphered and not this one; PARES has no decipherment. 'Undeciphered' on cryptiana means no contemporary decipherment, not unsolved; whether Tomokiyo or anyone else holds this easy alphabetical key is not known.
